sections.skill: Explain triangle congruence criteria with rigid motions

questions.skill: Explain triangle congruence criteria with rigid motions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEF have AB = DE, BC = EF, and angle B = angle E. A rigid motion moves B onto E and ray BA onto ray ED. Explain why A lands on D and C lands on F.
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangles ABC and DEF have AB = DE, BC = EF, and angle B = angle E. A rigid motion moves B onto E and ray BA onto ray ED.
Explain why A lands on D and C lands on F.
questions.correct_answer: A lands on D because AB = DE along the same ray. Because angle B = angle E, ray BC lands on ray EF (after a reflection if needed), and because BC = EF, C lands on F. So the triangles are congruent (SAS).

questions.skill: Explain triangle congruence criteria with rigid motions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Triangles PQR and STU have PQ = ST, QR = TU, and PR = SU. A rigid motion moves P onto S and Q onto T, with R and U on the same side of ST. Explain why R must land on U.
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangles PQR and STU have PQ = ST, QR = TU, and PR = SU. A rigid motion moves P onto S and Q onto T, with R and U on the same side of ST.
Explain why R must land on U.
questions.correct_answer: R lands where a circle of radius PR around S meets a circle of radius QR around T on that side of ST. U is that same point (SU = PR and TU = QR), and there is only one such point, so R lands on U (SSS).

questions.skill: Explain triangle congruence criteria with rigid motions
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D, AB = DE, and angle B = angle E. A rigid motion puts A on D and B on E, with C and F on the same side. Why must C land on F?
questions.prompt_markup:
Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D, AB = DE, and angle B = angle E. A rigid motion puts A on D and B on E, with C and F on the same side.
Why must C land on F?

choices.text: All triangles with a side of length AB are congruent.
A rigid motion stretches the sides until they match.
The rays from D and E at the equal angles cross at only one point, so C and F are the same point.

questions.correct_answer: The rays from D and E at the equal angles cross at only one point, so C and F are the same point.
